title: Causality-Based Conformal Imputation Correction with Non-Random Missing Labels

problem.claim: Learning from data with non-random missing labels can be biased, including in recommender systems where users choose whether to rate items.

gap.claim: Existing doubly robust guarantees require propensity or imputation accuracy for all units, imputation errors can create large bias, and effective evaluation of imputation quality for missing-label units is lacking.

contributions.claim: A model-agnostic framework assesses the accuracy of imputed labels and corrects imputations with large bias using conformal prediction.
The framework constructs prediction sets for units with unobserved labels and revises imputations that fall outside those sets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three real-world datasets and one semi-synthetic dataset showing the effectiveness of the proposed method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Non-random missing labels create challenges for unbiased learning, with user-controlled ratings as an example.
Reweighting, imputation, and doubly robust methods have been proposed, but their guarantees depend on strong accuracy assumptions.
Imputation errors can induce large bias, and imputation quality for missing-label units is difficult to evaluate.
The proposed framework uses conformal prediction sets to assess and correct biased imputations.
Experiments are reported across three real-world and one semi-synthetic dataset.

source_observation.claim: Conformal prediction is used to construct prediction sets for unobserved-label units and revise imputations outside those sets.

interpretation.claim: Prediction-set membership can serve as a model-agnostic signal for identifying potentially unreliable imputations.

application.claim: In missing-label learning workflows, use conformal prediction to screen imputed labels and target corrections to imputations outside the valid prediction set.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the validity conditions, calibration procedure, or performance limits of this use.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not state the assumptions required for conformal validity or correction effectiveness.
The abstract does not detail the causal model or how the method interacts with doubly robust estimation.
